en: Oṃ. May He protect us both together; may He nourish us both together;
may we work together with vigor.
May our study be radiant; may we never harbor hatred toward one another.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace.

In the land of Brahmāvarta, at the foot of the great Bhaṇḍīra fig tree, the great sages headed by Śaunaka had assembled for a long sacrificial session (*mahāsatra*). With sacrificial fuel in their hands and desiring to know the ultimate reality, they approached the long-lived Mārkaṇḍeya and asked: "By what means do you live so long, and by what means do you experience such bliss? ||1||
"By means of the knowledge of the supreme secret, the reality of Śiva," he said. ||2||
What is that knowledge of the supreme secret, the reality of Śiva?
In that regard, who is the deity?
What are the mantras?
What is recitation? What is the mudrā?
What is the ultimate goal?
What is the means for attaining that knowledge? What is the preliminary preparation? What is the offering?
What is the time?
What is that place? ||3||
He said:
"That by which Śiva, facing south, becomes directly perceived—that is the knowledge of the supreme secret reality of Śiva. ||4||
He who, at the time of the cessation of all things, having withdrawn everything into himself, rejoices or shines forth in the bliss of his own self-nature—he is God. 5.
In this regard, there are these verses concerning the secret of the mantras:
for the *medhā* mantra of Dakṣiṇāmūrti, Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*) and the *gāyatrī* is the meter (*chanda*).
The deity faces south;
the placement of the limbs is performed with a mantra. ||6||

First, having uttered "Oṃ" and "Namaḥ," then the word "Bhagavate," followed by the word "Dakṣiṇā," one should extract the word "Mūrtaye. Then one should utter the word "Medhām" and the word "Prajñām," with the pronoun "asmad" in the dative case.
Then, having uttered the seed-syllable of Vāyu, namely *Cham*, one should recite [the rest]; then follows the wife of Agni (*Svāhā*). This is the mantra consisting of twenty-four syllables. (7)

I praise Dakṣiṇāmūrti, who is in a state of meditation; whose color is like crystal or silver; who holds in the tips of his hands a rosary of pearls, a jar of nectar, a book, and the gesture of wisdom (jñānamudrā); who has a serpent as a waistband, the moon upon his crest, three eyes, and is adorned with various ornaments. 8.
The ritual placement (*nyāsa*) is performed with the mantra.
First, having uttered the beginning of the Vedas (*vedādi*), followed by the first vowel together with the *visarga*,
one should then extract the five-syllable [mantra] and the intermediate [syllable] together with the *visarga*.
This nine-syllabled mantra [is that which] first rescues its reciter. || 9 ||

May Bhava— the primordial one, seated beneath a banyan tree, with three eyes, his matted locks as white as milk and rivaling the crescent moon, his waist girdled by a serpent coiled like a cave, holding in his arms the *mudrā* that bestows auspicious wealth, an axe, and a deer, with one arm resting upon his knee, surrounded by sages such as Śuka— grant us purity of being.

The placement [of mantras] (nyāsa) by means of the mantra is the Brahmārṣinyāsa. Having uttered the Tāra (Om), Brūṃ, Namaḥ, Māyā (Hrīṃ), and Vāgbhava (Aiṃ), one should then utter the word "Dakṣiṇā," followed by the word "Mūrtaye. (11)
Bestow knowledge (JÑĀNAṂ), then the word "pada," and thereafter place the wife of fire (SVĀHĀ).
This eighteen-syllable mantra is hidden among all mantras. || 12 ||

May the Lord Dakṣiṇāmūrti protect us always—he whose limbs are pale with ashes, who wears a crescent moon, whose lotus-like hands shine with the knowledge-pearl, the rosary, the lute, and the book, who is beautiful with his yogic belt, who sits upon the seat of exposition, who is served by hosts of excellent sages, who is gracious, accompanied by a serpent, and clothed in an elephant hide. 13.
The placement is performed with the mantra.
[The Placement of the Brahman-sages: One should utter the Tāra (Oṃ), the supreme seed-syllable of Ramā (Śrīṃ), and "to Sāmbaśiva."
And for you, born of Fire, Manu consists of twelve syllables. || 14 ||

I praise Him who holds a lute, a book, and a rosary in His hands; whose neck has the hue of a cloud, who is enriched by the best of boons, who wears the lord of serpents as a girdle, who is served by sages such as Śuka and others, and who has made His nest beneath the banyan tree. 15.
Viṣṇu is the seer, Anuṣṭubh is the meter;
Dakṣiṇāsya is the deity.
The ritual placement (nyāsa) is performed with the mantra.
First, utter "Tāraṃ" (Oṃ), then "namo bhagavate tubhyaṃ vaṭapadaṃ," then pronounce the word "mūla," and thereafter extract the word "vāsine. (16)
Then [the word] *vāgīśāya*, followed by the word *mahājñānapada*; having uttered the word *dāyine*, one should extract the word *māyine namaḥ*. (17)
This king of mantras, composed in the Anuṣṭubh meter, is the most supreme among all mantras. || 18 ||

For the attainment of my desired goal, I meditate upon the Supreme Guru, the Lord of Bhavānī, who destroys ignorance; whose arms sport with a mudrā, a book, fire, and a serpent; whose face is serene; who is adorned with pearl necklaces; who shines with a crown radiant with a crescent moon; who is the primordial meaning of the words of the Primordial One; and who dwells at the edge of the banyan tree. 19.
The seal of silence:
that state of abiding in the realization "I am He" constitutes the final consummation. ||20||
The repetition of the mantra through non-differentiation from that [reality] is the means for attaining knowledge. ||21||
The preparation for the mind is its one-pointedness. ||22||
The offering of the movements of one's limbs is the *bali*. ||23||
Time is the three abodes. ||24||
The station of the "twelve-finger space" (dvādaśānta) is the locus. ||25||
Full of faith, they spoke to him again:
"How does its rising occur? What is its essential nature?"
"Or who is his lay follower? ||26||
He said:
"In the full vessel of awakening, filled with the oil of dispassion and provided with the wick of devotion, one should behold the lamp of knowledge. (27)
Indeed, in the essenceless darkness of delusion, it arises by itself;
having made dispassion the lower fire-drill and knowledge the upper fire-drill. (28)
To pacify the intense darkness [of ignorance], one should reveal the hidden meaning:
the son of Mṛkaṇḍu named Viveka, who has been transferred from the son of Moha-Bhānu. (29)
Established in his own true nature within his own bliss, he brings to life that which is bound by the noose of non-investigation into reality and afflicted by the fear of duality.

Wisdom is said to be the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā); he whose face is constantly turned toward that [wisdom] is declared by the exponents of Brahman to be Śiva facing the south (dakṣiṇābhimukha). || 31 ||
At the time of creation and so forth, the Lord Viriñci, having worshipped this [Lord], attained the power of creation;
having obtained his desired objects, he rejoiced in his heart. Thus, the blessed Creator becomes a worshiper who has performed worship.
He who studies this knowledge of the supreme secret, the reality of Śiva, becomes liberated from all sins.
He who knows this attains absolute liberation (*kaivalya*). Thus ends the Upaniṣad. 33.
Thus ends the Dakṣiṇāmūrti Upaniṣad.
Oṃ. May He protect us both together; may He nourish us both together;
may we work together with vigor.
May our study be brilliant; may we never harbor hatred toward one another.
Oṃ, peace, peace, peace!
